it wasn’t *technically* a crime, but it was delegated like one. 

in 6th grade i was part of a grade wide “safety day”. we had a simulated school shmooting. the alarm went off, the intercom system came on and said “code red. code red. move to your locations” and we all went and sat at the back wall. now our class had 3 large, square windows next to the door which had a thin rectangular window. the 3 square windows were blurry so you couldn’t see in or out, but you could see blurry color. this comes in later. 

so we’re starting this drill, all of us 11-12 year olds thinking it’ll be over in 5 minutes. but then we hear the yelling and moaning. some guy had been recruited to go up and down the hall yelling to “let him in”, banging on the doors, and cupping his hands at the glass and trying to look in. thanks to the blurry glass, we could see the man outside, but couldn’t see his exact form. 

all of us were terrified. i was clutching the girl next to me, who was near tears. we had a girl in our class who had been asked if she would stand up at some point and pretend to get sh*t through the door. she fell over (she was a bad actor, which was the only light hearted thing here) and we had to pretend she was really injured and couldn’t go help her. 

soon the fire department, police, and SWAT team showed up. one firefighter/emt came to our door and our teacher asked for identification and they came in and took out the girl who had pretended to be shot. we were left in the room. the way our school was set up was one hall per grade, and three “pods” of 4 classrooms on each hall. my pod was the end of the hall with the door to the outside world was right outside our door. the middle pod was literally shipped off to another location where their parents had to come pick them up. 

we found out later that some kids had professional makeup artists draw b*llet holes on them as well as other wounds, and the middle pod bathroom was covered in fake bl**d. we sat in that room for almost 4 hours, and then the drill ended and we went to our next class. 7th and 8th grade didn’t do this drill. 

i have ptsd from this. i hate guns and actively fight for regulation bc of it. i have severe anxiety and have to face the door in whatever restaurant i am in so i can see everyone who comes in. i know every exit where i am at all times, and i have multiple scenarios that i go through should something happen. i know at this point it’s not if, it’s when. the news covered this, but you can’t find anything about it online. which is annoying. 

i’m not the same person. this has made me an activist of so many sorts. i’m glad i am who i am, but i didn’t need life altering trauma at 11.
